correctness.rationale: Reconstructed four disjoint finite-field cases by choosing right-hand mth-power values for q≡1(mod m), counting (q−1)² + m(q−1)(q−m)² +2(q−1)(q−m−1)² +(q−1)(q−1−m)(q−2m)². Simplification yields asserted χ(q) for infinitely many good q and hence polynomial identity; Jacobson lattice good reduction follows for all but finitely many primes for fixed m. OS projectivized Poincaré identity gives b0..b3. Independently factored cubic discriminant into strictly negative −[3n^6+44n^5+292n^4+1040n³+1808n²+1408n+416], n=m−2, so irreducibly nonreal conjugate pair prevents free arrangement by Terao. Independent Sympy arithmetic checks verify original count and discriminant identity for small m and all polynomial coefficients, not replacing all-m proof.

evidence: Universal gain-graph deletion-contraction and characteristic-polynomial method is earlier, as are OS and Terao. These provide mechanisms to derive consequences once χ is computed, not the explicit all-m polynomial/nonreal-discriminant obstruction.

value.rationale: A uniform non-freeness theorem and explicit projective-complement topology for a natural published family containing a known Purdy counterexample are useful structural invariants. The family-specific cubic evaluation, especially its sign-uniform obstruction, is not merely the universal counting identity or a parameter substitution.

final_claim: For each m>=2, the central μ_m-gain 4-cycle hyperplane arrangement in C⁴ with ∏_{i=0,1;j=2,3}(x_i^m−x_j^m) has χ=(T−1)[T³+(1−4m)T²+(6m²−3)T−3m³−2m²+4m+1]. Its projective complement has Betti polynomial 1+(4m−1)t+(6m²−3)t²+(3m³+2m²−4m−1)t³. The arrangement is nonfree for every m>=2.
limitations: Only m>=2, complex 4-coordinate bipartite four-cycle arrangement; not all gain graphs or complement cohomology-ring structure.
The m3 Purdy-inequality violation and general gain-graph counting methods are established prior.
